RESEARCH

Data-driven synthesis,
from pores to performance.

We design nanoporous materials with data, make them with controlled synthesis, and connect their interfaces to molecular capture, catalysis and electrochemical energy. Every synthesis and every measurement becomes a data point for the next design.

데이터로 설계하고, 합성으로 구현하고, 계면에서 성능을 확인하는 연구.

HOW WE WORK

One loop, four stages.

See it in the material world ↗
01 · DESIGNDesign the space within.Pore architecture and interfaces are chosen as variables, not accidents: geometry, connectivity, surface chemistry.
02 · SYNTHESISGive the architecture form.Sol–gel, hydrothermal and solvothermal routes turn a design into a connected porous solid. Recipes are recorded as data.
03 · APPLICATIONSFrom interfaces to function.Adsorption, catalytic reactions and ion transport are measured on the same materials, under conditions that matter.
04 · AI DISCOVERYLearn. Redesign. Discover.Models trained on our own synthesis and performance data propose the next candidates, and the loop closes.

RESEARCH AREAS

Six subjects, one material world.

The six objects on the front page are the six things we work on. Each one below links back to the interactive scene.

01 · LEARNING

AI material design데이터 기반 소재 설계

Machine-learning models trained on synthesis conditions, structure and measured performance propose the next candidates. Active learning decides which experiment is worth running; literature mining builds datasets where none exist yet, with every extracted number traced back to its source.

The goal is not a model for its own sake but a shorter path from a question to a material in hand.

  • Active learning
  • Composition–property models
  • Literature mining
  • Bayesian optimization
  • Machine-learned potentials
02 · MAKING

Controlled synthesis제어된 합성

Sol–gel, hydrothermal and solvothermal routes to aerogels, alloys and oxides with controlled porosity, composition and interfaces. Supercritical and ambient-pressure drying preserve open frameworks; reproducible recipes are the raw material for the models above.

  • Sol–gel chemistry
  • Metal and oxide aerogels
  • High-entropy alloys
  • Supercritical drying
  • Hydrothermal / solvothermal
03 · STRUCTURE

Nanoporous architecture나노다공 구조

Pore geometry, connectivity and surface chemistry are design variables. We quantify them with gas physisorption, electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and connect texture to transport and reactivity.

  • N₂ / CO₂ physisorption
  • SEM · TEM
  • XPS
  • XRD
  • Texture–property relations
04 · CAPTURE

Selective adsorption선택적 흡착과 분자 포집

Electrified CO₂ capture and release, heavy-metal removal and molecular separation on porous interfaces where binding can be switched by potential, not by heat.

  • Electrified CO₂ capture
  • MnO₂ interfaces
  • Heavy-metal removal
  • Selective binding
05 · REACTION

Electrocatalysis전기화학 촉매

Hydrogen and oxygen evolution, ammonia oxidation and plasma-assisted electrochemistry on noble-metal-lean surfaces. Aerogel electrocatalysts give active sites open transport paths, so that what is measured is the chemistry and not the diffusion limit.

  • HER · OER
  • Water electrolysis
  • Ammonia oxidation
  • Plasma-electrochemistry
  • Noble-metal-lean catalysts
06 · ENERGY

Electrochemical energy전기화학 에너지

Porous electrodes where ion transport and interfacial reactions meet: electrolyzers, supercapacitors and battery electrodes built from hierarchical porous structures.

  • Electrolyzers
  • Supercapacitors
  • Battery electrodes
  • Ion transport
